name: Mining, Quarrying & Extractive Industries
saContext: Bushveld Complex PGM and chrome belt, Witwatersrand and Free State gold, Mpumalanga and Waterberg coal, Northern Cape iron ore and manganese, Kimberley and West Coast marine diamonds. Junior miners and black-owned small-scale operators sit in the same tree as the JSE-listed majors.

name: Platinum Group Metals & Chrome
saContext: Rustenburg, Marikana, Northam, Steelpoort and Mokopane. Post-demerger the listed PGM major trades as Valterra Platinum (JSE: VAL, formerly Anglo American Platinum).

name: PGM Mine Operations
saContext: Underground and open-pit PGM extraction, shaft and decline development, hoisting and winding.

name: Deep-Level Mechanised Stoping
saContext: Merensky reef mechanised stoping, trackless mobile machinery fleets, seismic management.

name: Platreef Bulk Mining
saContext: Mokopane / Platreef bulk mechanised operations and associated smelter feed contracts.

name: UG2 Reef Operations
saContext: Chromitite-hosted UG2 extraction, typically chrome credit driven.

name: PGM Concentration, Smelting & Refining
saContext: Concentrators, furnace and converter operations, base metals refineries and auto-catalyst precursor supply chains.

name: Auto-Catalyst Precursor Supply
saContext: Precious metal chemical supply into catalytic converter manufacturers, including component plants in the Eastern Cape and Gauteng automotive clusters.

name: Chrome Concentrate Production
saContext: Chrome extraction and concentrate for the domestic ferrochrome industry, largely supplying Nkangala and North West smelters.

name: Junior PGM Exploration & Development
saContext: The SMME end of PGM: prospecting right holders, junior developers and black-owned mining companies under MPRDA small-scale and artisanal provisions.

name: Black-Owned Junior & Small-Scale Mining
saContext: MPRDA small-scale mining permits, junior B-BBEE Level 1-2 operators and community-held mineral rights.

name: Gold
saContext: Witwatersrand basin, Free State goldfields and the Mpumalanga and Barberton greenstone belts. Deep-level cost pressure has pushed the sector into tailings retreatment, mechanised mining and closure economics.

name: Tailings Retreatment & Surface Dumps
saContext: Slimes dam and dump retreatment, re-processing of historic tailings, uranium by-product handling.

name: Gold Refining, Assaying & Minting
saContext: Rand Refinery-type refining, London Good Delivery bar production, Krugerrand minting.

name: Artisanal & Informal Gold Extraction
saContext: Zama zama operations in disused and working shafts. Recorded in the taxonomy because it is a real part of the registered and unregistered economy, not because it is legal: licensing status is captured separately under regulatory vectors.

name: Coal
saContext: Mpumalanga Highveld, Waterberg and Vryheid fields, split between export-grade and Eskom-supply contracts, with a long tail of small collieries supplying local industry.

name: Export-Grade Thermal & Coking Coal
saContext: Richards Bay Coal Terminal export chain, RB1/RB3 grades.

name: Eskom-Supply Domestic Coal
saContext: Tied collieries and short-term supply contracts feeding Mpumalanga power stations.

name: Small-Scale Collieries
saContext: Emerging black-owned collieries and contract mining permits supplying domestic industry.

name: Coal Hauling & Stockyard Logistics
saContext: Side-tipper road haulage and stockyard management; cross-referenced to TRA-ROAD-BULK.

name: Iron Ore, Manganese & Bulk Minerals
saContext: Northern Cape Kalahari manganese and iron ore fields (Sishen, Kolomela), rail-linked to Saldanha and Port Elizabeth.

name: Heavy-Haul Rail & Port Interface
saContext: Ore line slot allocation and port stockpile management; cross-referenced to TRA-RAIL.

name: Diamonds
saContext: Kimberley and Cullinan kimberlites, Namaqualand and West Coast alluvial and marine operations, plus the cutting and polishing beneficiation layer.

name: Diamond Cutting & Polishing
saContext: dtic-designated beneficiation activity concentrated around Johannesburg.

name: Battery & Critical Minerals
saContext: Vanadium, lithium pegmatites, copper, nickel, zinc, titanium and rare earths, plus mid-stream precursor processing driven by the just energy transition.

name: Quarrying, Aggregate & Industrial Minerals
saContext: The largest count of registered micro and small extractive entities in the country: aggregate quarries, sand pits and clay works supplying local construction.

name: Limestone & Dolomite
saContext: Agricultural lime, steel flux and cement feedstock.

name: Mining Services & Mine Support
saContext: Contract mining, drilling, shaft sinking, equipment supply and safety services. This is where most SMME participation in mining actually happens.

name: Mine Closure, Rehabilitation & Water
saContext: Closure planning, revegetation and acid mine drainage treatment - a growing SMME services market as legacy mines close.

name: Energy, Power & Green Transition
saContext: Eskom-dominated generation and transmission opening to Independent Power Producers through the REIPPPP bid windows, municipal distribution grids, and a very large SMME layer of solar and inverter installers filling the grid-decentralisation gap.

name: Generation & Independent Power Producers
saContext: IPP projects financed under REIPPPP bid windows, embedded generation for mines and industry, and thermal fleet operators.

name: REIPPPP / Bid Window IPPs
saContext: Project companies (SPVs) with 20-year PPAs, community and B-BBEE shareholding structures.

name: Solar PV IPP Project Company
saContext: Single-asset utility-scale solar project companies. Headcount is tiny while turnover and asset value are large, so the scale band must be driven by turnover rather than employees.

name: Project SPV & Shareholder Structuring
saContext: Deal structuring, community trusts and B-BBEE equity participation around a generation asset.

name: Embedded & Private Generation
saContext: Behind-the-meter generation for mines, malls and industrial parks, and wheeling arrangements.

name: Transmission, Distribution & Grid
saContext: National transmission, municipal distribution networks and the grid-connection bottleneck that shapes every renewable project.

name: Municipal Distribution Networks
saContext: Metro and municipality electricity distribution, prepaid metering revenue and non-technical losses.

name: Solar PV & Storage
saContext: From utility-scale EPC down to single-phase residential installers - the fastest-growing SMME cohort in the country after the 2022-2024 load-shedding boom.

name: Residential Solar & Inverter Installation
saContext: The grid-decentralisation gap: thousands of micro installers, many unregistered or newly formalised, working to SANS 10142-2 and NRS 097-2-1.

name: Compliant Residential PV Installation
saContext: Wireman's licence and CoC-issuing installers with municipal notification of the installation.

name: Unregistered / Informal Inverter Installers
saContext: Tracked explicitly: a large share of installations are done without CoC or municipal sign-off, which is a data-quality and safety flag rather than an exclusion.

name: Wind
saContext: Eastern Cape and Western Cape wind corridors, tower and blade localisation content debates, and O&M service firms.

name: Green Hydrogen & Derivatives
saContext: Boegoebaai and Saldanha green hydrogen and ammonia export projects, electrolyser supply chains and early refuelling infrastructure.

name: Petroleum, Fuels & Gas Downstream
saContext: Refining capacity rationalisation (Secunda, eThekwini), fuel wholesale and forecourt retail, LPG distribution and the NERSA-licensed petroleum supply chain.

name: Fuel Wholesale & Forecourt Retail
saContext: Site-licensed forecourt operators, many franchise or dealer-owned; cross-referenced to RTL-FUEL.

name: Energy Services, Installation & ESCO
saContext: Electrical contracting, performance contracting, metering and energy audits - the SMME backbone of grid decentralisation.

name: Agriculture, Forestry & Agribusiness
saContext: A barbell structure: large commercial co-operatives and export-led horticulture on one side, emerging and smallholder farmers on the other. Regional logistics hubs (Sundays River citrus, Stellenbosch wine, Bothaville grain, Tzaneen subtropics) determine where the registered entities cluster.

name: Field Crops
saContext: Maize triangle (Free State, North West, Mpumalanga), wheat in the Swartland and Free State, soy and sunflower expansion, KZN and Mpumalanga sugarcane.

name: Sugarcane Production
saContext: KZN North Coast and Mpumalanga cane growers and mill supply areas.

name: Horticulture & Export Fruit
saContext: Citrus Growers' Association export volumes, deciduous fruit in the Western Cape, subtropical expansion in Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

name: Citrus Production & Export
saContext: Sundays River Valley, Limpopo and Senwes-belt citrus, packed for EU and Asian markets.

name: Export Marketing & Cold Chain Logistics
saContext: Cross-referenced to WHL-COLD and TRA-COLD; port scheduling at Port Elizabeth, Cape Town and Durban.

name: Wine & Table Grapes
saContext: Cape winelands estates, co-operatives and cellars, plus the Northern Cape table grape industry around Upington.

name: Livestock & Animal Production
saContext: Beef and sheep farming across the interior, KZN and Mpumalanga feedlots, and the communal grazing economy.

name: Dairy
saContext: Southern Cape, KZN Midlands and Gauteng dairy belts, with a concentrated processor layer.

name: Poultry & Protein
saContext: Vertically integrated broiler producers plus a long tail of independent broiler houses and day-old chick suppliers.

name: Commodity Marketing, Storage & Co-operatives
saContext: Commercial mega-co-operatives (NWK, Senwes, AFGRI-type structures) that combine grain storage, input supply, mechanisation and financial services in one regional hub.

name: Agricultural Co-operatives
saContext: Member-owned regional co-operatives delivering inputs, storage, marketing and agri-finance.

name: Grain & Oilseed Commodity Trading
saContext: Safex-linked hedging, local buying and export merchandising.

name: Emerging & Smallholder Farming
saContext: Land reform beneficiaries, restitution and redistribution farms, and communal-area producers. Registration status varies from full CIPC registration to unregistered household production, so the entity-type vector carries the difference.

name: Smallholder Co-operative & Scheme Aggregation
saContext: Aggregation models that give smallholders packhouse, cold chain and export access.

name: Agricultural Finance & Crop Insurance
saContext: Production credit, crop insurance and structured commodity finance.

name: Forestry & Timber
saContext: Mpumalanga, KZN and Tsitsikamma plantations, community forestry partnerships and sawmilling.

name: Fisheries & Aquaculture
saContext: Quota-based marine rights, small-scale fishing permits, and a growing aquaculture sector.

name: Manufacturing & Industrial Processing
saContext: Automotive assembly clusters in the Eastern Cape and Gauteng, heavy chemicals and fuel synthesis at Secunda, steel and ferroalloys, and FMCG manufacturing that feeds the dominant retail chains.

name: Automotive & Component Manufacturing
saContext: OEM assembly plants (Volkswagen and Isuzu in Gqeberha, BMW in East London, Ford in Silverton, Mercedes-Benz in East London) with Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier parks around them, supported by APDP and then AIS incentive programmes.

name: Vehicle Assembly (OEM)
saContext: Complete vehicle assembly plants, largely export-led into European and UK markets.

name: Tier 1 Component Manufacturing
saContext: Direct-to-OEM suppliers, frequently foreign-owned subsidiaries with local B-BBEE participation.

name: Exhaust Systems & Catalytic Converters
saContext: The link back into the PGM value chain: converter manufacturing consumes locally refined platinum, palladium and rhodium.

name: Tier 2 & Sub-Assembly Manufacturing
saContext: Where most black-owned and SMME automotive participation sits, typically supplying Tier 1 plants.

name: Food, Beverage & FMCG Manufacturing
saContext: Branded FMCG manufacturers supplying Shoprite, Pick n Pay, SPAR, Woolworths and Massmart, plus private-label and township-scale producers.

name: Seafood Processing
saContext: Hake, lobster and abalone processing for export; cross-referenced to AGR-FISH.

name: Private Label & Co-Manufacturing
saContext: Contract manufacturing for retail house brands - a major SMME entry route into formal retail supply chains.

name: Chemicals, Petrochemicals & Fertiliser
saContext: Coal-to-liquids and gasification at Secunda, ammonia and fertiliser at Richards Bay and Sasolburg, and specialty chemical suppliers into mining and water treatment.

name: Metals, Steel & Fabrication
saContext: Primary steel at Vanderbijlpark and Newcastle, aluminium at Richards Bay, and a dense layer of fabricators, foundries and precision machine shops.

name: Precision Machining & CNC
saContext: Jobbing machine shops - a classic mid-market and SMME cluster around Gauteng and Durban industrial areas.

name: Mineral Beneficiation & Smelting
saContext: Ferrochrome, ferromanganese, titanium slag and PGM refining - the beneficiation layer the state has pushed for two decades.

name: Plastics, Rubber & Packaging
saContext: Rigid and flexible packaging for FMCG, with extended producer responsibility obligations now driving a recycling content market.

name: Textiles, Apparel, Leather & Footwear
saContext: KZN and Western Cape clothing manufacturing under the Retail-Clothing, Textile, Footwear and Leather master plan, including the informal cut-make-trim layer.

name: Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices
saContext: SAHPRA-regulated manufacturing, generic and ARV production, and medical consumables.

name: Defence & Aerospace Manufacturing
saContext: Armour, energetics and aerospace component manufacturing, largely NCIA-regulated with localisation requirements.

name: Light Manufacturing & Jobbing Shops
saContext: Small workshops, welding shops and repair services - high informal participation, usually EME or QSE for B-BBEE.

name: Retail, FMCG & Consumer Goods
saContext: One of the most concentrated retail markets in the world at the top (Shoprite, Pick n Pay, SPAR, Woolworths, Massmart, Mr Price, TFG) and one of the most fragmented at the bottom, where tens of thousands of spaza shops and street traders serve township and rural demand.

name: Supermarket & Hypermarket Chains
saContext: Checkers, Pick n Pay, Woolworths Food, SPAR and Boxer formats.

name: Value & Discount Grocery
saContext: Boxer, Shoprite Usave and Jumbos-type value formats serving lower-income trade areas.

name: Voluntary Trading Groups & Symbol Group Franchisees
saContext: SPAR-type voluntary group membership where the trading entity is independently owned.

name: Fresh Produce Markets & Greengrocers
saContext: Municipal fresh produce market floors (Joburg, Tshwane, Durban) and independent greengrocers.

name: Credit & Instalment-Sale Retail
saContext: The TFG, Lewis and Pepkor model where retail and account-based credit are one business; cross-referenced to FIN-LEND.

name: Pharmacy & Health Retail
saContext: Chain and independent pharmacies plus dispensing doctors; dispensing licences regulated by SAHPRA.

name: Forecourt & Convenience Retail
saContext: Dealer-owned and franchise forecourts, frequently black-owned under fuel licensing and transformation requirements.

name: Franchise Operations
saContext: Franchise and Business Opportunity Regulation under the Consumer Protection Act; the dominant SMME route into branded retail and food service.

name: Spaza / Informal Retail & Township Trade
saContext: The informal trade economy: spaza shops, street traders, hawkers and buy-back points. Often unregistered or sole proprietorships, cash-based, and supplied through informal wholesale depots rather than formal retail supply chains.

name: Informal Wholesale & Depot Supply to Spaza
saContext: Cash-and-carry break-bulk and depot operators supplying township retail; cross-referenced to WHL-FMCG-SPAZA.

name: Stokvel & Burial Society Retail Trade
saContext: Bulk-buying stokvels that purchase groceries and groceries-plus-appliances in December; cross-referenced to FIN-INFORMAL-STOKVEL.

name: Wholesale, Distribution & Supply Chain Trade
saContext: Cash-and-carry and break-bulk wholesale, cold chain infrastructure, industrial MRO distribution, and the informal wholesale depots that supply the spaza economy.

name: Cold Chain Storage & Handling
saContext: Commercial cold storage measured in pallet positions rather than headcount, serving retail, food manufacturing, fisheries and export horticulture.

name: Transport, Freight & Logistics
saContext: A road-dominated freight system (roughly four fifths of tonne-kilometres), constrained rail and ports, a huge minibus taxi passenger economy, and an owner-driver long tail that makes this sector one of the largest sources of small registered entities.

name: Bulk Tipper & Side-Tipper Operations
saContext: Coal, chrome, aggregate and grain bulk movement; cross-referenced to MIN-COAL-HAUL.

name: Owner-Driver & Small Fleet Operators
saContext: One to five truck operators, frequently financed through vehicle finance and contracted to larger carriers.

name: Temperature-Controlled Distribution
saContext: Multi-temperature fleet operations serving retail distribution centres, food manufacturing and export packhouses.

name: Minibus Taxi Associations & Operators
saContext: A semi-formal economy dominated by associations rather than companies: many operating entities are not CIPC-registered, and revenue is cash-based. Entity type and informality vectors must be used instead of assuming a company record.

name: Financial Services, Banking & Insurance
saContext: A deep dual economy: a sophisticated formal sector led by the Big Five banks and the large insurers, sitting alongside stokvels, burial societies and informal lenders that hold most of the savings behaviour in low-income communities. FSCA, SARB and FIC regulation applies unevenly across that divide.

name: Banking - Universal & Retail
saContext: The Big Five ecosystem (Standard Bank, FNB, Absa, Nedbank, Capitec) plus mid-tier, mutual and cause-related banks. All are PRCB-registered under the Banks Act.

name: Universal Retail Banks (Big Five)
saContext: Standard Bank, FirstRand/FNB, Absa, Nedbank and Capitec: the dominant deposit and lending franchise in the country.

name: Corporate & Investment Banking
saContext: RMB, Absa CIB, Nedbank CIB, Standard Bank CIB and Investec: structured finance, trade, project finance and mining finance.

name: Mid-Tier, Mutual & Cause-Related Banks
saContext: African Bank, Bidvest Bank, HBZ, VBS-type mutual banks and postbank.

name: State-Owned Banks & Development Banks
saContext: Postbank and Land Bank; cross-referenced to FIN-DFI and PUB-SOC.

name: Co-operative Banks
saContext: Co-operative Banks Act institutions serving stokvels, savings clubs and township finance.

name: Digital & Challenger Banking
saContext: Licensed digital-first banks (TymeBank, Bank Zero, Discovery Bank) competing on cost-to-income and app-led acquisition.

name: Licensed Digital / Challenger Banks
saContext: Full bank licence, branchless distribution, typically unlisted private companies rather than JSE-listed groups.

name: Branchless & Retail-Partner Bank Models
saContext: Retail-partner deposit-taking models such as in-store banking partnerships.

name: Non-Bank & Alternative Lending
saContext: NCA-registered credit providers outside the bank perimeter. Note that the National Credit Act treats most SMME credit as consumer credit where the turnover is very low, which shapes how these firms document affordability.

name: Vehicle & Asset Finance
saContext: WesBank, Absa Vehicle and Asset Finance, MFC-type captives and independent truck finance.

name: SME & Business Lending
saContext: The underserved middle: business lending to registered small and medium enterprises, often with ESD-linked risk sharing.

name: Insurance & Underwriting
saContext: Life, short-term and health underwriting, plus the very large funeral cover and funeral parlour economy which is one of the biggest SMME clusters in financial services.

name: Funeral Services & Funeral-Cover Administration
saContext: The funeral ecosystem the user must map: parlour operators are overwhelmingly micro and small enterprises, while policy administration and group schemes sit with licensed insurers and administrators.

name: Funeral Parlour Operator
saContext: Family-owned parlours, typically EME or QSE, frequently also distributing funeral policies as FSPs or representatives.

name: Funeral Policy Underwriting & Administration
saContext: Licensed insurers and administrators running group funeral schemes, including for stokvels and employers.

name: Brokerages & Intermediary Services
saContext: FSCA-licensed FSPs and representatives; a large population of micro brokerages.

name: Payments, FinTech & Financial Infrastructure
saContext: The fastest-growing formal fintech cluster, centred on Cape Town and Johannesburg, spanning switching, wallets, merchant acquiring, remittances and open banking.

name: Merchant Services, POS & Payment Acceptance
saContext: Includes informal-trade acceptance products built for spaza and street-trader cash-to-digital conversion.

name: Informal Finance: Stokvels, Societies & Informal Lending
saContext: Community-based financial institutions that rarely hold CIPC registration. Data engineers must model them without requiring a registration number, using association and constitution evidence instead.

name: Stokvels & Savings Societies
saContext: Rotating and accumulation stokvels, often affiliated to national stokvel associations and increasingly served by formal banking products.

name: Burial Societies
saContext: Community burial cover societies, frequently unregistered but with written constitutions and bank accounts.

name: Informal Money Lenders (Mashonisa)
saContext: Payday and salary-advance lending outside the NCA registration perimeter.

name: Development Finance & Impact Capital
saContext: State DFIs and impact funds that finance SMMEs, black industrialists and infrastructure, each with its own B-BBEE and transformation mandate.

name: Information Technology, Telecommunications & BPO
saContext: Infrastructure giants at the top, systems integrators in the middle, and a large and fast-growing SMME layer of software studios, agencies and BPO operations clustered in Cape Town and Johannesburg. BPO is one of the biggest formal job creators for youth.

name: Telecommunications Operators
saContext: Mobile network operators, fixed-line and converged providers, MVNOs and wholesale capacity sellers, all ICASA-licensed.

name: Mobile Network Operators
saContext: Vodacom, MTN, Telkom Mobile, Cell C and Rain: spectrum-licensed national networks.

name: MVNOs & Retail Resellers
saContext: A rapidly growing set of licensed resellers, many with informal-trade distribution into township markets.

name: Pan-African Network Operators
saContext: South African-headquartered operators running fibre and capacity across the continent, frequently unlisted group structures.

name: Systems Integration & Managed Services
saContext: Large integrators and their subcontract ecosystems; the traditional destination for enterprise IT headcount.

name: ERP Implementation & Support
saContext: SAP, Microsoft Dynamics and Oracle partner ecosystems; cross-referenced to the SA SAP ERP track in this repository.

name: CRM & Marketing Technology Implementation
saContext: Salesforce, Microsoft and HubSpot partners; cross-referenced to the SA Salesforce ecosystem track in this repository.

name: Software Development & Product
saContext: The SMME software economy: product companies, dev studios, mobile shops and staff-augmentation firms concentrated in Cape Town's Woodstock/Claremont corridor and Johannesburg's northern suburbs and Sandton.

name: Software Development Agencies & Studios
saContext: Two to fifty person studios - the core SMME cohort, frequently QSE or EME and heavily reliant on contract work.

name: Bootcamp Graduates & Founder-Led Micro Studios
saContext: Micro entities formed by recent coding bootcamp graduates; cross-referenced to the SA Hackathon Census talent pool in this repository.

name: BPO, Contact Centres & Shared Services
saContext: A major youth-employment engine, supported by the Global Business Services incentive, with large campuses in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban and Gqeberha.

name: Construction, Engineering & Property
saContext: CIDB-graded contractors from grade 1 emerging firms to Tier 1 groups, consulting engineers, specialist trades and the property development and investment layer. Construction sector code B-BBEE thresholds differ from the general codes.

name: Construction Contracting & Delivery
saContext: CIDB grading (grades 1-9) determines tender eligibility, so grade is a first-class attribute alongside scale band.

name: Emerging & Small Contractors (CIDB 1-4)
saContext: The target of most public-sector ESD and local-content programmes; high churn and frequent deregistration risk make CIPC status monitoring essential.

name: Engineering Services & Consulting
saContext: ECSA-regulated consulting engineers and specialist engineering firms serving mining, petrochemical, power and water sectors. Many cluster around the Free State and Mpumalanga industrial corridors.

name: Petrochemical Plant Maintenance & Shutdown Services
saContext: The Sasolburg, Secunda and Sasolburg-Sasol corridor service market: planned shutdowns, statutory inspections and mechanical maintenance contracts.

name: Boiler & Pressure Vessel Work
saContext: OHS Act pressure equipment regulations require accredited inspection authorities, so compliance status is a gating attribute.

name: Water & Sanitation Works
saContext: Municipal water and sanitation delivery, a major route for emerging contractor participation.

name: Self-Build & Informal Construction
saContext: Informal settlement upgrading, owner-builder activity and unregistered construction labour.

name: Specialist Trades & Subcontracting
saContext: The trades layer where micro enterprises dominate: plumbing, electrical, roofing, painting, glazing, steel fixing and scaffolding.

name: Aggregate & Sand Supply
saContext: Cross-referenced to MIN-QUARRY.

name: Property Development & Investment
saContext: Developers, listed REITs and funds, estates agencies, and the township property economy that sits largely outside formal title.

name: Estate Agencies & Property Services
saContext: PPRA-regulated agencies and independent agents; a large micro-enterprise population.

name: Township & Informal Settlement Property Economy
saContext: Backyard rental, informal letting and untitled land - economically significant but absent from formal registers.

name: Cleaning & Hygiene Services
saContext: Bargaining-council regulated with minimum wage floors; one of the largest employers of micro and small service firms.

name: Security & Guarding Services
saContext: PSIRA-registered firms; cross-referenced to PRO-SEC.

name: Professional, Advisory & Business Services
saContext: Legal, accounting, consulting, recruitment, marketing and corporate services. Extremely high micro-enterprise density: sole practitioners, bookkeepers and small consultancies dominate the count even though the revenue concentrates in a few large firms.

name: Accounting, Audit & Tax
saContext: IRBA-registered auditors, SAICA and SAIPA practices, and a very large bookkeeping and payroll layer that services the SMME economy. Cross-referenced to the SA Accounting & Finance Talent Pool in this repository.

name: Bookkeeping, Payroll & Accounting Services
saContext: The micro-enterprise backbone of SMME compliance: monthly bookkeeping, VAT201 and EMP501 submissions.

name: CIPC Registrations & Company Secretarial
saContext: Annual returns, director changes, beneficial ownership filings and deregistration rescues - directly relevant to the CIPC status vector in this taxonomy.

name: Environmental & Sustainability Consulting
saContext: EIA practitioners, water use licensing and just-transition advisory; cross-referenced to MIN-REHAB.

name: Labour Broking & Temporary Employment Services
saContext: Registered with the Department of Employment and Labour; a major formal employer of entry-level staff.

name: Training Providers, Learnerships & SETA Services
saContext: QCTO and SETA-accredited providers; B-BBEE skills development spend flows here.

name: Public Relations & Communications
saContext: Note the PR sector code sets B-BBEE QSE thresholds from R5m rather than the general R10m.

name: Guarding & Manned Security
saContext: PSIRA-regulated; one of the largest employers in the country by headcount.

name: Health, Life Sciences & Wellness
saContext: A two-tier system: private hospital groups and medical schemes serving roughly a fifth of the population, and the public system with municipal and provincial facilities. NHI implementation reshapes the payer landscape.

name: Public Hospitals & Provincial Facilities
saContext: Cross-referenced to PUB-DEPT.

name: Pharmaceutical Retail & Distribution
saContext: Cross-referenced to RTL-PHAR and WHL-MED.

name: Occupational Health & Industrial Testing
saContext: Mine and factory medical surveillance, a steady SMME services market.

name: Traditional & Complementary Health
saContext: Traditional health practitioners registered through the THPC, with substantial informal practice.

name: Tourism, Hospitality & Events
saContext: Lodges, hotels, restaurants, tour operators and guides. The tourism sector code sets its own B-BBEE EME and QSE thresholds (R5m and R45m) rather than the general ones.

name: Bars, Taverns & Shebeens
saContext: Liquor licensing is provincial; a large share of taverns operate informally or on provisional licences.

name: Public Sector, State-Owned Companies & Utilities
saContext: National and provincial departments, state-owned companies, municipalities and their entities, water boards and regulators. PFMA and MFMA governance applies, procurement is B-BBEE-gated, and these entities are the largest single buyers of SMME services.

name: State-Owned Companies & Entities
saContext: Eskom, Transnet, PRASA, Denel, SAA, SANRAL, IDC and similar, many carrying large balance-sheet and service-delivery obligations.

name: Energy & Utility SOCs
saContext: Eskom and its generation, transmission and distribution divisions; cross-referenced to ENR.

name: Transport & Logistics SOCs
saContext: Transnet freight rail, ports and pipelines, PRASA and SANRAL.

name: Industrial & Development SOCs
saContext: Denel, IDC and similar industrial holdings; cross-referenced to FIN-DFI.

name: Municipalities & Municipal Entities
saContext: Eight metros, forty-four district municipalities and the local municipalities beneath them, plus municipal entities delivering electricity, water and waste.

name: Metropolitan Municipalities
saContext: City of Johannesburg, City of Cape Town, eThekwini, City of Tshwane, Ekurhuleni, Nelson Mandela Bay, Buffalo City and Mangaung.

name: District Municipalities
saContext: Includes Fezile Dabi District Municipality, within which Sasolburg sits in Metsimaholo Local Municipality.

name: Municipal Entities & Service Utilities
saContext: Joburg Water, City Power-type entities and municipal development agencies.

name: Regulators, Agencies & Public Institutions
saContext: The bodies whose status fields the metadata schema records: CIPC, SARS, SANAS, NERSA, FSCA, SEDA, the CSD, CIDB, PSIRA, PPRA, NHBRC and the Municipal Demarcation Board.

name: Development & Support Agencies
saContext: SEDA, SEFA, NEF and provincial enterprise development agencies that fund and register SMMEs.

name: Education, Training & Skills Development
saContext: Public and private schools, universities, TVET colleges, private FET providers, SETAs and a very large ECD micro-enterprise population.

name: Early Childhood Development
saContext: Crèches and ECD centres, overwhelmingly micro enterprises, many operating from homes without full registration.

name: Private Occupational Training Providers
saContext: QCTO and SETA-accredited providers delivering artisans, learnerships and bootcamps.

name: Civil Society, Foundations & Community Organisations
saContext: NPOs, NPC structures, foundations, community-based organisations, faith bodies, sport structures and labour organisations. Registration is dual-track: NPO Act registration with the Department of Social Development sits separately from CIPC registration as an NPC.

name: Corporate & Development Foundations
saContext: The vehicles through which B-BBEE socio-economic development points are spent.

name: Trusts & Community Trusts
saContext: Mining and IPP community trusts created as licence or bid-window conditions.

name: Employer Organisations & Business Associations
saContext: Chambers of commerce, industry bodies and business associations, including township business forums.

name: Retail Deposit & Transaction Banking
saContext: Mass-market transactional accounts; Capitec and FNB dominate the volume end of this niche.

name: SME & Business Banking
saContext: The relationship-managed end of the scale-band taxonomy: small and medium enterprises with turnover between R10m and R250m.

name: Fully Licensed Branchless Bank
saContext: TymeBank-type model: bank licence, retail-partner distribution, no branch estate. Typically a private company rather than a JSE-listed entity.

name: Neobank & App-Only Challenger
saContext: Bank Zero-type model: fully digital onboarding and lending.

name: Black-Owned & Transformation-Focused SME Lending
saContext: Black industrialist and transformation-mandated lending books, often blended with DFI risk capital.

name: Enterprise & Supplier Development Lending
saContext: B-BBEE ESD-driven supply chain finance extended to SMME suppliers of large corporates.

name: Accumulation & Grocery Stokvels
saContext: Year-end grocery and appliance stokvels; cross-referenced to RTL-INFORMAL-STOKVEL for the retail side of the same transaction.

name: Stokvel Administration & Fintech Platforms
saContext: Formal administrators and platforms providing bank accounts, debit orders and record-keeping to informal savings groups - the bridging niche between the formal and informal economies.

name: Burial Society Administration
saContext: Cross-referenced to FIN-INS-FUNERAL-POLICY where the society buys a group funeral policy.

name: Commercial Maize Production
saContext: Free State, North West and Mpumalanga maize triangle producers delivering to co-operative silos.

name: Citrus Packhouse & Export Preparation
saContext: The regional logistics hub node: packhouses feeding Port Elizabeth, Cape Town and Durban cold chains.

name: Full-Service Agricultural Co-operative
saContext: The NWK and Senwes model: input supply, storage, grain marketing, mechanisation, fuel and financial services under one member-owned structure in a regional hub.

name: Emerging Export-Oriented Growers
saContext: Emerging farmers brought into export value chains through aggregation and packhouse access.

name: Franchise-Operated Grocery Stores
saContext: Independently owned trading entities operating under a chain brand - the franchise operator layer the brief asks to map.

name: Voluntary Group Member Store
saContext: SPAR and OK-type member stores: the legal entity is the member, not the group, so taxonomy assignment must be at member level.

name: Independent Spaza Shop
saContext: Frequently a sole proprietorship or unregistered household business in a residential structure.

name: Multi-Site Township Convenience Chain
saContext: Formalising operators running several township sites, often CIPC-registered and VAT-voluntary-registered.

name: Multi-Site Franchise Operator
saContext: Franchisees holding several outlets, typically mid-market by turnover but small by headcount per site.

name: Township Depot & Break-Bulk Operator
saContext: The wholesale supply chain node for informal retail: bulk purchase, break-bulk, cash sales, delivery routes.

name: Voice Contact Centre Campus Operator
saContext: Large multi-hundred-seat campuses, frequently in Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban and Gqeberha.

name: Collections & Insurance Servicing BPO
saContext: Cross-referenced to FIN-SVC-COLLECT: the same activity viewed from the technology side.

name: Global Business Services Captive Centre
saContext: Captive shared-service centres of multinationals operating from South Africa under GBS incentives.

name: Green Ammonia Export Project
saContext: Boegoebaai and Saldanha-type projects, typically large SPVs with consortium shareholding.

name: Taxi Association Operating Entity
saContext: Associations are the governing unit of the minibus taxi industry and are frequently not CIPC-registered companies.

name: CIDB Grade 1-2 Emerging Contractor
saContext: Entry grading, usually restricted to small public-sector packages and ESD-supported work.

name: Export-Oriented Vehicle Assembly Plant
saContext: Eastern Cape and Gauteng assembly plants producing predominantly for European and UK export markets.

name: Synthetic Fuel & Chemical Conversion Plant
saContext: Secunda-type coal and gas conversion operations, with a dense local service-contractor economy around shutdowns.
